text:
(2) A defence statement that discloses an alibi must give particulars of it, including—
(a) the name, address and date of birth of any witness the accused believes is able
to give evidence in support of the alibi, or as many of those details as are
known to the accused when the statement is given;
(b) any information in the accused’s possession which might be of material
assistance in identifying or finding any such witness in whose case any of
the details mentioned in paragraph (a) are not known to the accused when the
statement is given.

(3) For the purposes of this section evidence in support of an alibi is evidence tending to
show that by reason of the presence of the accused at a particular place or in a particular
area at a particular time he was not, or was unlikely to have been, at the place where
the offence is alleged to have been committed at the time of its alleged commission.
